newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Slovenia shares rise 0.08 pct to record high.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia shares rise 0.08 pct to record high.

text.p: Slovenian shares extended their bull run on Friday, with the blue chip SBI index rising 0.08 percent to hit a fresh all-time high of 1,651.96.
Traders said the index was buoyed by demand for shares in BTC and Kovinotehna. The 11-share SBI index has hit a record high for the third consecutive day.
"The index went up mainly due to a rise in the shares of BTC and Kovinotehna, while Lek and SKB fell prey to a technical correction after recent steep gains," one trader said

The index has now risen 39.4 percent since the beginning of the year, primarily driven by strong foreign demand for drug maker Lek and leading private bank SKB, and traders see little reason for the uptrend to end soon.

Traders said parliament's rejection on Thursday of a new cabinet proposed by prime minister-designate Janez Drnovsek had little impact on the bourse, although the country may now be heading for premature elections.

"Slovenia is not portrayed as a country of political risk, therefore the current political situation does not present a major influence for foreign or domestic investors," said Danilo Grasic head of the investment sector of Slovenia's branch of Austrian bank Creditanstalt.
Toni Apollonio, an analyst at bank A Banka, predicted the positive trend would continue, backed by the expectation of strong earnings from some of the blue chip companies.
Although Lek and SKB fell today on what market participants said was natural technical correction, other shares on the index performed well and buoyed the index.

"Shares will continue rising as long as foreigners are prepared to buy shares of Lek and SKB and after Krka is listed that will also attract some new investments," Andrej Kavcic, a trader at brokerage Ilirika said.
Lek's main rival Krka will list its shares on Monday and become the second pharmaceutical company on Ljubljana bourse.
The market's turnover fell to 480.2 million tolars from 877.2 million. Overall 10 shares rose and eight fell, while seven were untraded.
Drug company Lek's A issue had the highest turnover, easing one percent to 33,590 tolars on volume of 6,411 shares.
Trading company Kovinotehna was the biggest gainer, jumping 8.0 percent to 540 tolars on volume of 2,256 shares.
Bank UBK led the day's decliners, falling 6.25 percent to 6,000 tolars on volume of 10 shares.
